_guide: Lines the game builds sentences from. Lines live in named groups; the game asks a group for a line.
A line is either plain text, or { "text": ..., "when": {...}, "weight": 2 }.
{crew}          the crew member in this scene (shows their name). {place}, {item}, {biome}, {weather}, {time} work the same way.
In crew lines, {crew} is one crew member (or you). {crew.role} is their profession, {crew.trait} their trait, {crew.wear} what they wear, {crew.gear} what they carry, {ship} the ship's name.
{crew.name}     a part of it. {Crew} = capital first letter.
{crew.they} {crew:laughs|laugh}   after a pronoun: 'she laughs', 'they laugh'. After a name just write the verb: '{Crew} laughs'.
{a:item}        adds 'a' or 'an': 'a brass lantern', 'an old map'.
{@smell}        drops in a line from the group called smell, so you can build sentences from small pieces.
[soft|quiet|still]   picks one of these at random.
when (optional): the line is only used when everything in it matches.
"biome": "desert"        only on deserts.  ["desert", "salt"] = any of them.  "!rain" = anything but rain.
"temp": ">0.6"          numbers: above 0.6 (or "<0.3" for below). temp, water, life go from 0 to 1.
"crew.tags": "nervous"  a part of something: here, the crew member's trait tags.
weight (optional): 2 = picked twice as often, 0.5 = half as often.
Groups with the same name in different files are joined, so you can make a new file in content/ for your own lines
(add it to CONTENT_FILES in js/boot.js). Try lines in tools/text-preview.html.
Biomes are often plural ("rust plains"), so don't put a verb or "a" straight after {biome}: write "the light over the {biome} turns", not "the {biome} turns".

arrive: The ship settles down on the {biome}. Everything is [quiet|still|hushed] for a moment.
{Place} looks [smaller|bigger|stranger] than it did from orbit.

arrive.text: At {time} the light over the {biome} turns [pink|gold|violet]. {@smell}
Rain drums on the hull. Nobody is in a hurry to step outside.
Frost creeps across the windows as soon as the engines go quiet.
The air shimmers with heat. {Crew} fans {crew.themself} with a map.

smell: The air smells of [rain on stone|burnt sugar|old books|cold metal].

smell.text: Something here smells like salt and lightning.

crew_notice.text: {Crew} jumps at a noise, then laughs at {crew.themself}.
{Crew} turns over every stone in sight. Most of them are just stones.
{Crew} says this planet is too [cold|loud|purple] and then writes three pages about it.

item_moment: {Crew} holds up {crew.their} {item} to get a better look.

item_moment.text: {Crew}'s {item} catches the light. Something out on the {biome} seems to notice.
{Crew} pulls {crew.their} {item} a little tighter against the wind.
{Crew} lights {crew.their} {item}, and the dark steps back a little.
{Crew}'s {item} keeps {crew.them} dry while everyone else gets soaked.

ship_life: {Crew} spends the session reorganising {crew.their} bunk. It looks exactly the same afterwards.
{Crew} writes a long letter to someone back home and doesn't send it. Not yet.
{Crew} [hums|whistles|sings] something old in the corridor. Nobody asks what it is. Everybody knows the tune by the end.
{Crew} falls asleep in the observation deck with a book open on {crew.their} chest.
{Crew} makes tea for everyone. It's slightly too strong, which is how the {ship} likes it.
{Crew} spends an hour watching the stars slide past the window and calls it work.

ship_life.text: {Crew} polishes {crew.their} {crew.gear} until {crew.they} can see {crew.their} own face in it.
{Crew} plays a few notes on {crew.their} {crew.gear}. The engines seem to hum along.
{Crew} sketches the corridor, the galley and the back of somebody's head.
{Crew} pours everyone something warm from {crew.their} {crew.gear}.
{Crew} fixes a squeaky hinge with {crew.their} {crew.gear} and then fixes three more out of momentum.
{Crew} pulls {crew.their} {crew.wear} a little tighter. The ship is cold tonight.
Someone compliments {crew}'s {crew.wear}. {Crew.they} {crew:pretends|pretend} not to be pleased.
{Crew} tunes the engines by ear and declares them "happy".
{Crew} cooks something new. It is purple. It is delicious. Nobody asks.
{Crew} runs the same test three times and gets three different answers. {Crew.they} {crew:looks|look} delighted.
{Crew} flies a little loop just because the stars look nice from upside down.
{Crew} talks a passing freighter into swapping a bag of apples for a song.
{Crew} checks everyone's temperature. Prescription: more naps.
{Crew} tells the story of the last world over dinner, and makes it sound even better than it was.
{Crew} waters the little plants in the galley and tells each of them it's doing well.
{Crew} redraws the last map from memory. It's better than the real one.
{Crew} paints a tiny planet on the galley door. Then another. It's turning into a solar system.
{Crew} practises one song over and over until the whole crew can hum it.
{Crew} jumps at the sound of the coffee machine, then pretends {crew.they} meant to.
{Crew} grumbles about the noise, the cold and the soup, then helps with all three.
{Crew} naps through an entire course correction. Twice.
{Crew} finds a snack nobody knew the ship had.
{Crew} tells a joke so bad that the whole galley groans, then laughs for ten minutes.
{Crew} labels the spice rack. And the labels. And the drawer the labels came from.
{Crew} spends the session at the window, watching nothing in particular, very happily.

arrive_crew: {Crew} is first to the window when {place} comes into view.

arrive_crew.text: {Crew} is out of the airlock before the ramp is all the way down.
{Crew} takes one look at {place} and starts drawing it.
{Crew} fills a sample jar before anyone else has their boots on.
{Crew} lifts {crew.their} {crew.gear} for a better look at the {biome}.
